A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAP despite the changed title. All 24 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original localization experiments, component ablations, generalization analyses and inference measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Aachen Day-Night evaluation, further comparisons and ablations, and mixed-precision inference measurements.

M1.justification: The core 3DGS, Transformer, two-branch adversarial training and pose-refinement procedures remain. Appendix E.2 replaces the stated auxiliary triplet loss with VICReg and adds rejection of synthetic images with BRISQUE scores at least 50 in scenes with nearby objects. These are localized changes within the retained framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds a daytime-training/nighttime-testing Aachen subset and the Court scene in Cambridge Landmarks, substantially extending appearance-shift evaluation. The original indoor, driving and Cambridge coverage remains. St. George’s Basilica was already evaluated in v1 Appendix J; its appearance in v2’s main text is a relocation.

E2.justification: The Cambridge comparison adds LENS, DFNet/ACE plus GS-CPR, and DFNetref; 7-Scenes adds CoordiNet + LENS, marepo and GS-CPR variants. v2 also evaluates DFNetGS. Conversely, the Cambridge table drops the NeFeS30 row, and MARS drops DFNet because its NeRF training was unsuccessful. Renaming NRP to PPR is not itself a comparator change.

E3.justification: The new Aachen protocol uses center cropping, standardized cameras, reconstructed COLMAP labels, 246 daytime training images, 13 nighttime test images and translation errors in COLMAP units. Retained training specifications also change: discriminator learning rate 0.0002 to 0.0001, batch size 12 to 8–12, resizing rules and the stopping criterion. Additional experiments compare augmentation policies, scene representations and AMP inference configurations; these reported changes do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds LENS-style pose-sampling and NeRF-to-3DGS replacement ablations in Tables 7 and 10, plus an appearance-augmentation removal comparison on Aachen in Table 3. The validation-loss curves in v1 Figure 1 disappear. Existing component, void-zone, data-density, image-quality, deblurring and spatial-generalization analyses largely remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty across runs. Both retain median, mean, minimum and maximum localization-error summaries; the added experiments do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Reported RAP averages change from 58 cm/1.39° to 56 cm/1.28° on Cambridge, 5 cm/2.51° to 5 cm/1.90° on 7-Scenes with SfM poses, and 45 cm/0.78° to 28 cm/0.60° on MARS. The reported 7-Scenes DSLAM RAPref average changes adversely from 2.8 cm/0.91° to 2.97 cm/1.47°. New benchmark, ablation and AMP results are added, and train/test PSNR assignments are reversed in the image-quality table. Method and setting revisions prevent treating these as isolated same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical content of Equations 1–12 and the appendix rendering and regularization equations is retained, with appendix equations renumbered from I–III to 13–15. Neither version develops formal guarantees or proofs. The newly named auxiliary loss is not accompanied by a new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds scaling synthetic data to enable interpolation and extrapolation by closing separate data and learning gaps. v2 redefines the central contribution around appearance diversity exploited through adversarial training and explicitly claims day-to-night robustness where previous APR methods fail. Generalizability and the two-branch framework remain central, but the principal scientific emphasis and claimed applicability change substantially.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving poor rendering quality under broad pose sampling and reduced 3D consistency when replacing NeRF with 3DGS. Appendices E.2, I and N add substantive qualifications about quality filtering, camera-intrinsic ambiguity, resolution sensitivity and accuracy loss at metric scale in large scenes. The earlier Shop rolling-shutter explanation disappears. Existing SE(3) overlap arguments and failure cases are retained through relocation.

D1.justification: v2 documents FP16 AMP, the BRISQUE threshold and the Heads/320 × 240 inference setting. It corrects the discriminator description from BCE to MSE and the regression-head hidden-layer wording, making them consistent with equations already present in v1. The code notice changes from a promised future release to directing readers to code; the PDFs alone do not verify availability.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges that LENS previously attempted appearance augmentation, revising v1’s positioning of earlier augmentation as pose-only. It explicitly relates RAPref to GS-CPR and expands discussion of CoordiNet/LENS refinement. References supporting marepo, VICReg, BRISQUE and Aachen are added, while several general data-scaling examples disappear. These changes materially revise the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution list are substantially rewritten around appearance diversity and adversarial learning. Benchmark discussions and appendix sections are reordered, the two spatial-generalization discussions exchange main-text/appendix placement, and limitations move into an expanded appendix section. Terminology changes include NRP to PPR.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned and reduced to one column, losing its training-loss panel. The Cambridge visualization is redrawn with Court, benchmark tables gain substantial row/column changes, and new ablation tables and an Aachen appearance figure appear. Numerous existing figures and tables move, including both generalization diagrams and the appendix galleries.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for appearance robustness through targeted Aachen evaluation and policy/representation ablations, expands relevant baselines, and states important camera and resolution limitations. Removing MARS DFNet scores from unsuccessful training and correcting inconsistent implementation descriptions also improve credibility. The gains are moderated by the small custom nighttime test and reporting problems, including Table 7’s 22.47° average despite per-scene errors of 1.15–3.50°. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
